- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >0.33 negative values) and model shows upward trend, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >60.00), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast rise to +2–3% above peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If official supply net is negative and bullish events are low, model overestimates mean; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent 7-day average.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated bearish swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast to catch reversal.  
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (e.g., >3/30d), model underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.0% to reflect supply uncertainty.  
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome shows mean reversion after spike, model often fails to correct; apply 1–2% downward correction at 10–15d mark post-spike.
